short: The chancellor who became prime minister just in time for the financial crisis.
full:
Gordon Brown had been chancellor for ten years, the longest unbroken tenure in the office's modern history, before succeeding Tony Blair unopposed in June 2007. Within months came a run on Northern Rock, the first on a British bank since the 1860s, and a year later the collapse of Lehman Brothers.

His response was to recapitalise the banks directly with public money rather than merely buy their bad assets, a model quickly copied in Washington and across Europe, and to push a coordinated fiscal stimulus through the G20 summit he hosted in London in April 2009. The cost was a deficit above ten per cent of national income and an argument about austerity that shaped the following decade. The parliamentary expenses scandal, a difficult relationship with his own cabinet and a chance remark caught on a live microphone marked the 2010 campaign, and Labour lost its majority in May.
